title: CLI surfaces SqualifyException.Code
lead: The CLI exits 3 when the library refuses with `SqualifyErrorCodes.FirstRecordTooLong` (the `--max-first-record-bytes` ceiling), so a script can tell it apart from every other error, which stays exit 1. The stderr message and the rule that a failure writes nothing are unchanged. **Not in this slice:** other error codes or exit codes; adding the code to the descriptor or to the stderr text; changing library API.
**Owner decision (2026-11-03):** distinct exit code 3; exit 1 stays for every other error; stderr unchanged. Exit 2 is left unused because .NET command-line parsers commonly use it for usage errors.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: sq-73 added `SqualifyException.Code` and `firstRecordTooLong`; the CLI still maps every error to 1, so a script cannot react to a first record that is too long (for example, retry with a larger ceiling) without parsing the message. Once 1.1.0 ships, scripts will depend on the current "1 on any error" behavior, so the distinction is cheaper to add now.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/squalify.Cli/CliApp.cs`: `RunAsync` catches `SqualifyException` and returns 1; return a named constant 3 when `ex.Code == SqualifyErrorCodes.FirstRecordTooLong`.
- `tests/squalify.Cli.Tests/CliTests.cs` (the exit-code tests; the existing first-record test, if any).
- `docs/user-guide.md` (the "Exit codes" bullet, line 29 at spec time), `docs/getting-started.md` (line 119), `README.md` (line 36); `docs/examples.md` if a script example claims "non-zero is one thing".

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `FirstRecordTooLong_ExitsWithThree`: a file whose first record exceeds `--max-first-record-bytes` exits 3.
2. `FirstRecordTooLong_WritesTheMessageToStderrAndNothingToStdout`: the stderr text is the exception message as before; stdout is empty.
3. `FirstRecordTooLong_LeavesAnExistingOutputFileUntouched` with `-o`.
4. `OtherErrors_StillExitWithOne`: a missing file, a directory and a usage error exit 1 (pinned beside the new tests; the usage case is not a `SqualifyException`).

Mutation checks: return 1 for the coded case, and tests 1 must go red; return 3 for every `SqualifyException`, and test 4 must go red.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. At start, re-anchor the files and lines above against the code in the worktree.
2. Write the tests and watch each fail for the stated reason.
3. Implement in `CliApp.RunAsync`; keep the exit-code values in one place (named constants).
4. Docs in the same change: user guide "Exit codes" (0 success; 3 when the first record exceeds `--max-first-record-bytes`; 1 on any other error), `getting-started.md`, `README.md`, and an example in `examples.md` if it fits. Check the user guide's changelog section for a place that lists CLI behavior changes in 1.1.0 and add one line if it has one; the library API labels do not change.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release --filter "Category!=Corpus&Category!=Large"` (every test project's summary line)
- `dotnet format squalify.sln --verify-no-changes`
- Run the built CLI on a file whose first record exceeds a small `--max-first-record-bytes`: exit 3, message on stderr, no output file; a missing path still exits 1.
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/sq-81` on branch `sq-81`. No agent commits. After the gate returns `VERDICT: PASS`, the orchestrator commits `sq-81: CLI error code`.
